topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of how cancer arises through an interplay of intrinsic mutations, genetic predisposition, environmental exposures, and epidemiological variation.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens contribute to cancer development, detailing oncogenic mechanisms and the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce direct and indirect DNA damage through metabolic activation and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the principles of tumour promotion, the two-stage model of carcinogenesis, and host developmental susceptibility in cancer progression.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer risk.

topics.label: Conclusion and lecture summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture's key concepts.
